programme.title: Sound Waves: The Symphony of Physics
programme.desc: Helen Czerski investigates the science behind familiar sounds as well as those humans cannot hear. At the Palace of Westminster, she teams up with scientists to carry out measurements using state-of-the-art lasers to reveal how Big Ben vibrates to create pressure waves in the air at particular frequencies. She also explores the science of the voice, inviting soprano Lesley Garrett to sing I Dreamed A Dream inside an MRI scanner to reveal how her vocal tract acts as a resonator, amplifying and shaping the sound from her larynx

programme.title: Elizabeth Taylor: A Tribute
programme.desc: A programme dedicated to the Oscar-winning actress, with friends, family and co-stars sharing their memories and looking back on her career, as well as her humanitarian work and much-publicised personal life. Featuring contributions from Liza Minnelli, Joan Collins, Pierce Brosnan, Angela Lansbury, David Frost, Larry King, Robert Hardy, Barry Norman and Richard Burton's nephew Guy Masterson

programme.title: The Secret Rules of Modern Living: Algorithms
programme.desc: Without people noticing, modern life has been taken over. Algorithms run everything, from search engines on the internet, to satnavs and credit-card security - they even help people travel the world, find love and save lives. Here, mathematician Marcus du Sautoy demystifies this hidden world by showing some of the most essential algorithms. He reveals where these 2,000-year-old problem-solvers came from, showing how they work, what they have achieved and how they are now so advanced they can even program themselves

programme.title: Today at the Test
programme.desc: England v Pakistan. Highlights of day five of the Third and Final Test in the series from Edgbaston in Birmingham. The teams had not met in a Test at this venue since 2016, when England prevailed by 141 runs, and the hosts have won four and lost four of the eight matches played in this format here since

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Highlights from a summer of extraordinary music at the world's biggest classical music festival. From Berlioz to Beethoven, Miles Davis to Marvin Gaye, this is a special selection of the best musical moments from across the season, including performances by Sheku Kanneh-Mason, Jess Gillam, Ladysmith Black Mambazo and more. Presented by Petroc Trelawny, Georgia Mann, Katie Derham, Nick Mohammed, Andi Oliver and Clive Myrie

programme.title: Selina Thompson Remembers - Salt
programme.desc: The performance artist looks back at the 2021 adaptation of her dramatic monologue, revealing the changes needed to create something for TV that retained the power of the stage play. She discusses the influences behind the show, the need to engage the audience as part of the ritual and the consequences of performing something so physically and emotionally draining

programme.title: Salt
programme.desc: Performance artist Selina Thompson re-creates her award-winning and deeply personal monologue about her journey by cargo ship, retracing the route of the transatlantic slave trade. Throughout the film, Thompson explores her painfully difficult but ultimately redemptive exploration of the Atlantic triangle in a cathartic pilgrimage through grief, race and identity

programme.title: Stephen Tompkinson Remembers - The Deep Blue Sea
programme.desc: The actor looks back on his role in the BBC's 1994 adaptation of the acclaimed Terence Rattigan play, directed by pioneer of British film Karel Reisz and also starring Colin Firth, Ian Holm and Penelope Wilton. He explains why he seized the opportunity to join the cast, recalls the challenges involved and describes in particular what it was like to witness in person Penelope Wilton's central performance as Hester, described by critics as one of the decade's greatest acting masterclasses

programme.title: The Deep Blue Sea
programme.desc: Hester is rescued by a neighbour after attempting suicide in the flat she shares with her younger lover, ex-RAF pilot Freddie Page. Karel Reisz's 1994 adaptation of Terence Rattigan's play, starring Penelope Wilton, Colin Firth, Ian Holm, Stephen Tompkinson, Geraldine Somerville and Carmel McSharry

programme.title: Nature and Us: A History Through Art
programme.desc: James Fox considers the way art over the past 100 years reflects how nature was swapped for progress in the first half of the 20th century, before rediscovering its beauty in the decades following the Second World War, and how today's artists are reimagining the human race's future relationship with nature

programme.title: Flying Scotsman from the Footplate
programme.desc: A guide to life on the footplate of the nation's favourite steam engine. Cameras are placed aboard locomotive 60103 as it travels along the Severn Valley, cutting through stunning landscapes on a journey from Bridgnorth to Kidderminster. The 'cab cameras' capture veteran driver Roger Norfolk and fireman Ryan Green in action as they talk through the mechanics and challenges of operating this national treasure. Needless to say, things sometimes get hot on the footplate and not everything goes exactly to plan

programme.title: Steve Backshall's Extreme Mountain Challenge
programme.desc: Part two of two. The naturalist reaches the peak of one of Venezuela's tepui mountains, before joining a party of Italian cavers as they venture into the unexplored caverns within. Inside, they discover strange wildlife and evidence of the geological forces that give the tepuis their unusual shape. Finally, the team returns to the ground by abseiling down the Angel Falls, the world's highest waterfall

programme.title: Earth's Seasonal Secrets
programme.desc: The last in a set of four documentaries exploring wildlife and plants throughout the year focuses on the spring, when hibernating animals awake and many species search for mates. The programme features footage of grizzly bear cubs, the mating dances of grebes, flowers growing in the desert and swifts embarking on marathon journeys

programme.title: Britain's Lost Masterpieces
programme.desc: Bendor Grosvenor and Emma Dabiri visit Brighton Museum to investigate who painted two neglected pictures of religious subjects. Plus, Emma investigates how Brighton's Royal Pavilion ended up an empty shell, ransacked and sold to the local council

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson hosts the sixth heat of the quiz, with four contenders answering questions on the specialist subjects of George Orwell, the history of costume from 1600, Rome, and the Common Market

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson presides over another duel of words and wits as Diana Quick, Robert Powell, Anouska Hempel and Nigel Havers join captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell. First broadcast in 1979

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Chris Lintott and the team explore the extraordinary engineering, both on Earth and millions of kilometres above it in space, that is transforming modern astronomy and revealing parts of the cosmos once thought forever beyond human reach

programme.title: This Cultural Life
programme.desc: John Wilson speaks to the Turner Prize-winning artist and curator about her creative influences

programme.title: Romancing the Stone: The Golden Ages of British Sculpture
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke tells the stories of sculptors John Flaxman, Francis Chantrey and Alfred Gilbert, who bucked trends in the 18th and 19th centuries. He examines the technical breakthroughs behind their key works - such as carving in marble with a pointer machine and the lost-wax technique - which were produced at a time of increased interest in sculptural projects to celebrate the size of the British Empire

programme.title: The Boleyns: A Scandalous Family
programme.desc: Documentary charting the rise and fall of the Boleyns, a story of love, sex and betrayal told from the family's unique perspective. The first edition reveals how patriarch Thomas Boleyn was determined to elevate his family name, with his ambitions for his three children taking them to the heart of the Tudor court

programme.title: The Crime I Can't Forget
programme.desc: In 2013 a Romanian woman approached the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) claiming a gang had forced her into prostitution. Other victims need to be found to gather crucial evidence, but inside the brothels, fear and grooming had silenced vulnerable women. Detectives Rachel Miskelly and Dougie Grant turned to digital forensics and pieced together the movement of victims across country borders. They recall how, in a groundbreaking human trafficking investigation, the PSNI join forces with Swedish authorities, Europol, and Romanian agencies to bring the leaders of this crime gang to justice
